Visualising location and bird species

For visualising purposes we use adapt code by Mentesana, Hau, D’Amelio, Adreani, & Sánchez-Tójar, (2025), available on the accompanying GitHub repository.

The following code chunk is used to set up the workspace and load (or install) all required packages to replicate the generatation of figures and tables presented in our manuscript.

## Setting up workspace using pacman
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}

## installing orchaRd from GitHub
if (!requireNamespace("orchaRd", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ## installing orchaRd from GitHub
  pacman::p_install_gh("daniel1noble/orchaRd", ref = 'main')
}

## Install/load required packages
pacman::p_load(
  cowplot,
  ggraph, # visualising author network
  gt, # suppl 
  here,
  igraph, # visualising author network
  maps,
  metafor,
  orchaRd,
  patchwork,
  purrr,
  tidyverse)

For the purpose of this map, longitude and latitude of the study area manually added to the dataset. They are saved to dataset_analysis$population_location as they were extracted from the respective papers. If not provided by the authors, a general location was manually selected. Note, coordinates are used for visualising only.

  • Load datasets
## Load data for plotting a location map
## -----------------------------------------------------------

# Loading cleaned dataset
dataset_analysis <- read_csv(here::here("data/04_data_analysis/dataset_analysis.csv"))
## Rows: 274 Columns: 71
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (35): paper_ID, fulltext_screening, variable_note, authors, population_l...
## dbl (35): year_publication, Observation_ID, experiment_ID, group_ID, repeate...
## lgl  (1): fulltext_notes
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
## Split population_ID into location and country
dataset_analysis[c('Location','Country')] <- str_split_fixed(dataset_analysis$population_ID, ',', 2)

## set coordinates for sampling locations
data_coordinates <- data.frame(
  Location = unique(dataset_analysis$Location),
  Lat_Location = c(51.50, 38.41, 40.45, 45.40, 52.39, 37.18,
                   40.53, 54, 39.05, 51.57, 48, 42.54, 39.95,
                   40.13,28.10,52.06,60.39),
  Long_Location = c(19.29,-9.02,-3.50, -64.10, 6.05, -3.11,
                    -4.01, -124, -76.81, -2.26, 11, 8.91,
                    -75.16, -8.27, 107.10, 8.25, 5.32))

## Let's now merge the datasets by the location names
dataset_analysis <- dataset_analysis %>%
  left_join(data_coordinates, by = "Location")

## Count how many times each Location appears in the full dataset
location_counts <- dataset_analysis %>%
  group_by(Location, bird_species) %>%
  summarise(size.freq = n())
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by Location and bird_species.
## ℹ Output is grouped by Location.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(Location, bird_species))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
# I will subset the data base so that I get one row per Location AND bird_species.
# Like this, I get one point per location independently of the number of effect sizes
# we have per place.
dataset_analysis_unique_rows <- dataset_analysis %>%
  distinct(Location, bird_species, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Merge the counts into the unique rows dataset
dataset_analysis_unique_rows <- dataset_analysis_unique_rows %>%
  left_join(location_counts, by = c("Location", "bird_species"))

# create data for world coordinates using  
# map_data() function 
world_coordinates <- map_data("world") 

# create world map using ggplot() function 
# geom_map() function takes world coordinates as input to plot world map 
fig_map <- ggplot(world_coordinates, aes(x = long, y = lat)) + 
  geom_map(map = world_coordinates, 
           aes(map_id = region), 
           color = "white", fill = "#D9EAF7") + 
  geom_point(data = dataset_analysis_unique_rows, 
             aes(x = Long_Location, y = Lat_Location,
                 size = size.freq, colour = bird_species),
             alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_size(range = c(1, 2.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#00B0BE","#FFB255",  "#FF8CAE", 
                               "#F47A00", "#98C127","#003A7D","#7E4794")) +
  
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#00B0BE","#FFB255",  "#FF8CAE", 
                                 "#F47A00", "#98C127","#003A7D","#7E4794")) +
  guides(size = "none", alpha = "none",
         colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1.5), keywidth = 0.4,
                               keyheight = 0.4)) +
  labs(x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude",
       col = "Bird Species") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 15, r = 15, b = 5, l = 5),  
        legend.position = c(1.02, 0.42),
        legend.justification = c("right", "bottom"),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

# To add the zoomed in map.. to show the points more clearly
zoom_map <- ggplot() + 
  geom_map(data = world_coordinates, map = world_coordinates,
           aes(map_id = region),
           color = "white", fill = "#D4D4D4") +
  geom_point(data = dataset_analysis_unique_rows,
             aes(x = Long_Location, y = Lat_Location,
                 size = size.freq, colour = bird_species),
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.2),
             alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_size(range = c(1, 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#00B0BE","#FFB255",  "#FF8CAE", 
                                 "#F47A00", "#98C127","#003A7D","#7E4794")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 20), ylim = c(25, 65)) +  # Northern Hemisphere
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.background = element_rect(color = "white", fill = "white"),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 1))
## Warning: The `size` argument of `element_rect()` is deprecated as of ggplot2 3.4.0.
## ℹ Please use the `linewidth` argument instead.
## This warning is displayed once per session.
## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
## generated.
geographic_distribution <- ggdraw() +
  draw_plot(fig_map) +
  draw_plot(zoom_map, x = 0.11, y = 0.21, width = 0.20, height = 0.28) +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 1.2))

print(geographic_distribution)

## Save image file
ggsave(here::here("figures/Figure_Distribution.png"),
       plot = geographic_distribution, height = 100, width = 170, units= 'mm', dpi = 600)

Visualizing author network

# Sun Aug 31 19:25:52 2025 ------------------------------
# Show code, but eval = FALSE

## Loading cleaned dataset
# Sun Aug 31 19:26:35 2025 ------------------------------
# The folliwing file is not found, assume same as above?!
# dataset_analysis<- read_csv(here::here("data/03_data_cleaning/dataset_analysis.csv"))

clean_author <- function(name) {
  name %>%
    str_replace_all(",", "") %>%   # remove commas
    str_squish() %>%              # remove excess whitespace
    str_to_title()                # standardize case (optional, if needed)
}

# Apply cleaning to first and last author fields
author_roles <- dataset_analysis %>%
  distinct(paper_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(paper_ID, authors, bird_species) %>%
  mutate(
    author_list = str_split(authors, ";\\s*"),
    first_author = map_chr(author_list, 1),
    last_author = map_chr(author_list, ~ tail(.x, 1))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    first_author=case_when(
      first_author == "Polo, V" | first_author == "Polo V" ~ "Polo V.",
      first_author == "Soler J J" ~ "Soler J. J.",
      first_author == "Glądalski, M" ~ "Gladalski M.",
      first_author == "Gwinner, H" | first_author == "Gwinner H" ~ "Gwinner H.",
      TRUE ~ as.character(first_author)
    )) %>%
  mutate(
    last_author=case_when(
      last_author == "Veiga J P" ~ "Veiga J. P.",
      TRUE ~ as.character(last_author)
    )
  )

# 2. Create Core Author Pairs (First → Last)
author_pairs_core <- author_roles %>%
  select(paper_ID, first_author, last_author) %>%
  rename(from = first_author, to = last_author) %>%
  filter(from != to) %>%
  count(from, to, name = "weight")

# 3. Build Author Graph
author_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(author_pairs_core, directed = TRUE)

# 4. Assign Dominant Bird Species to PIs (last authors)
author_species <- author_roles %>%
  select(last_author, bird_species) %>%
  group_by(last_author, bird_species) %>%
  count() %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 1) %>%
  distinct(last_author, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Add species as vertex attribute
V(author_graph)$bird_species <- author_species$bird_species[
  match(V(author_graph)$name, author_species$last_author)
]

# 5. Optional: Scale node size by number of papers per author
author_paper_counts <- author_roles %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(first_author, last_author), names_to = "role", values_to = "author") %>%
  count(author, name = "paper_count")

# Add paper count attribute
V(author_graph)$paper_count <- author_paper_counts$paper_count[
  match(V(author_graph)$name, author_paper_counts$author)
]

# Replace NAs with small size for isolated authors
V(author_graph)$paper_count[is.na(V(author_graph)$paper_count)] <- 1

# 6. Plot with ggraph
ggraph(author_graph, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight), alpha = 0.4, color = "grey50") +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = bird_species, size = paper_count)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.3, 2)) +
  scale_size(range = c(3, 10)) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Author Collaboration Network by Bird Species",
       size = "Paper Count") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

Intercept only model

Orchard plot for overall effect of green nest material on fitness using lnRR and SMDH

# Loading models for SMDH and lnRR
intercept_lnRR <- readRDS(here::here("model/intercept_lnRR.rds"))
intercept_SMDH <- readRDS(here::here("model/intercept_SMDH.rds"))

# Plot for lnRR
intercept_lnRR_plot <- orchaRd::orchard_plot(
  intercept_lnRR,
  mod = "1",
  group = "paper_ID",
  trunk.size = 0.3,
  branch.size = 2,
  twig.size = 0.5,
  alpha = 0.2,
  xlab = "Effect size (lnRR)", 
  fill =  T,
  k.pos = c(0.53,0.6,0.6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = "#98C127") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = "#98C127" ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
    legend.position = c(0.98, 0.05),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0),
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "Intercept")
## Scale for fill is already present.
## Adding another scale for fill, which will replace the existing scale.
## Scale for colour is already present.
## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.
# Plot for SMDH
intercept_SMDH_plot <- orchaRd::orchard_plot(
  intercept_SMDH,
  mod = "1",
  group = "paper_ID",
  trunk.size = 0.3,
  branch.size = 2,
  twig.size = 0.5,
  alpha = 0.2,
  xlab = "Effect size (SMDH)",
  fill = TRUE,
  k.pos = c(2,0.6,0.6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = "#F47A00") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = "#F47A00") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
    legend.position = c(0.98, 0.05),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0), 
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(x = "Intercept")
## Scale for fill is already present.
## Adding another scale for fill, which will replace the existing scale.
## Scale for colour is already present.
## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.
# Combine using patchwork
Figure_intercept <- intercept_lnRR_plot / intercept_SMDH_plot +
  plot_annotation(tag_level = c("A","B"))
print(Figure_intercept)

## save image file
ggsave(here::here("figures/Figure_overall_effect.png"), 
       plot = Figure_intercept, height = 150, width = 170, units = "mm", dpi = 600)

Hypothesis meta-regression

# Loading models for SMDH and lnRR
lnRR_hypothesis <- readRDS(here::here("model/lnRR_hypothesis.rds"))
SMDH_hypothesis <- readRDS(here::here("model/SMDH_hypothesis.rds"))

# Plot lnRR meta-regression on hypothesis
lnRR_hypothesis_plot <- orchard_plot(mod_results(
  lnRR_hypothesis,
  mod = "Hypothesis",
  group = "paper_ID"),
  trunk.size = 0.25,
  branch.size = 1,
  twig.size = 0.5,
  alpha = 0.4,
  xlab = "") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#FF8CAE", "#003A7D", "#7E4794")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#FF8CAE", "#003A7D", "#7E4794")) +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Effect size (lnRR)") +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8),
    legend.position.inside = c(0.99, 0.01),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0), 
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Both","Courtship","Parental Care"))
## Warning in mod_results(lnRR_hypothesis, mod = "Hypothesis", group =
## "paper_ID"): It is recommended that you fit the model with an intercept.
## Unanticipated errors can occur otherwise.
## Scale for colour is already present.

  labs(x = "", y = "Effect size (SMDH)") +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8),
    legend.position.inside = c(0.99, 0.01),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0), 
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) +

## Warning in mod_results(SMDH_hypothesis, mod = "Hypothesis", group =
## "paper_ID"): It is recommended that you fit the model with an intercept.

## Scale for colour is already present.

SMDH_hypothesis_plot <- SMDH_hypothesis_plot +

Now we combine these plots

## I am going to remove the y ticks from the SMDH plots to make it smaller..
SMDH_design_plot <- SMDH_design_plot +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

SMDH_time_gnm_addition_plot <- SMDH_time_gnm_addition_plot +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

# Combine using patchwork
Figure_design_time_gnm_addition <- 
  ((lnRR_design_plot + SMDH_design_plot) /
     (lnRR_time_gnm_addition_plot + SMDH_time_gnm_addition_plot)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
print(Figure_design_time_gnm_addition)

## save image file
ggsave(here::here("figures/Figure_design_time_gnm_addition.png"),
       plot = Figure_design_time_gnm_addition, height = 240, width = 250, units = "mm", dpi = 600)

## I am going to remove the y ticks from the SMDH plots to make it smaller..
SMDH_parasite_plot <- SMDH_parasite_plot +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

SMDH_birds_plot <- SMDH_birds_plot +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

SMDH_trait_plot <- SMDH_trait_plot +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

# Combine using patchwork
Figure_parasite_birds_trait <-
  ((lnRR_parasite_plot + SMDH_parasite_plot) / 
     (lnRR_birds_plot + SMDH_birds_plot) / 
     (lnRR_trait_plot + SMDH_trait_plot)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")

Table for all fitness proxies included in the analysis

pacman::p_load(readr,knitr, tidyverse, gt)
dataset_analysis <- read_csv(here::here("data/04_data_analysis/dataset_analysis.csv"), show_col_types = F)

fitness_proxies<-dataset_analysis%>%
  select(c(fitness_proxy_cleaned,paper_ID, proxy_decision, Hypothesis))%>%
  # make proxy names clean and pretty
  mutate(fitness_proxy_cleaned = fitness_proxy_cleaned %>%
      str_replace_all("_", " ") %>%
      str_to_title())

fitness_proxies_table <- fitness_proxies %>%
  group_by(fitness_proxy_cleaned, Hypothesis) %>%
  summarise(
    k = n(),
    n = n_distinct(paper_ID),
    proxy_decision = first(proxy_decision),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Hypothesis, desc(k))

fitness_proxies_table <- fitness_proxies_table %>%
    mutate( 
    # Add * to proxies used only in sensitivity analyses
    fitness_proxy_cleaned = if_else(
      proxy_decision == "sensitivity-analysis",
      paste0(fitness_proxy_cleaned, "*"),
      fitness_proxy_cleaned
    ),
      Hypothesis = factor(Hypothesis, levels = c("CH","PCH","both"))) %>%
    group_by(Hypothesis) %>%
    mutate(row = row_number(),
           entry = sprintf("%s: %d (%d)", fitness_proxy_cleaned, k, n)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(Hypothesis, row, entry) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Hypothesis, 
                values_from = entry, 
                values_fill = list(entry = " ")) %>%
    select(CH, PCH, both) %>%
    gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    CH   = "Courtship Hypothesis",
    PCH  = "Parental Care Hypothesis",
    both = "Both Hypotheses"
  ) %>%
    tab_header(title = "Fitness Proxies included in the meta-analysis",
               subtitle = "Proxy: Effect Sizes (Papers), * indicates the fitness proxies included only in a sensitivity analysis")

  
# Saving as an image
gtsave(fitness_proxies_table, here::here("tables/SA_fitness_proxies_table.pdf"))

Table for all the excluded proxies

merged_data_extraction <- read_csv(here::here("data/03_data_cleaning/merged_data_extraction.csv"), show_col_types = F)

dataset_analysis <- read_csv(here::here("data/04_data_analysis/dataset_analysis.csv"),
                             show_col_types = F)

excluded_proxies<- merged_data_extraction %>%
  filter(fulltext_screening == "included" |
         is.na(fulltext_screening) |
         fulltext_screening == "NA") %>%
  filter(proxy_decision== "exclude")%>%
    mutate(Category = "Completely excluded")

SA_only_proxies <- dataset_analysis %>% 
  filter(proxy_decision == "sensitivity-analysis") %>%
    mutate(Category = "Sensitivity-analysis only")

excluded_proxies_table<-bind_rows(excluded_proxies,SA_only_proxies)%>%
  select(Category, fitness_proxy, proxy_comment, paper_ID)%>%
  mutate(
    fitness_proxy = fitness_proxy %>%
      # Remove days
      str_remove_all("\\(day\\s*\\d+\\)") %>%
      # Remove years
      str_remove_all("\\d{4}") %>%   
      # Remove any leftover parentheses
      str_remove_all("\\(.*?\\)") %>%
      # Replace underscores with spaces
      str_replace_all("_", " ") %>%
      # Same name for all sex ratio proxies
      {case_when(
        str_detect(.,regex("sex\\s*ratio|proportion\\s+of\\s+males", TRUE))~"Sex Ratio",
        str_detect(.,regex("glucose", TRUE))~"Glucose Concentration",
        TRUE ~ .)}%>%
      # Trim any extra spaces
      str_trim() %>%
      # Capitalize each word
      str_to_title()) %>% 
  group_by(Category, fitness_proxy) %>%
  summarise(
    k = n(),
    n = n_distinct(paper_ID),
    proxy_comment = first(proxy_comment),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  arrange(factor(Category, levels = c("Completely excluded", 
                                    "Sensitivity-analysis only")), desc(k))


excluded_proxies_table <- excluded_proxies_table %>%
  select(
    Category,
    `Fitness Proxy` = fitness_proxy,
    `Effect Sizes (k)` = k,
    `Articles (n)` = n,
    `Reason for Exclusion` = proxy_comment
  ) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Category") %>%       # << This creates the subheadings
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Fitness proxies excluded from the meta-analysis**")
  ) %>%
  cols_align("center", columns = c(`Effect Sizes (k)`, `Articles (n)`)) %>%
  cols_align("left", columns = c(`Fitness Proxy`, `Reason for Exclusion`)) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = 10,
    data_row.padding = px(2),
    heading.align = "left",
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
    row.striping.background_color = "#F7F7F7"
  )

# Saving as an image
gtsave(excluded_proxies_table, here::here("tables/SA_excluded_proxies_table.png"))

# Table for lnRR Values
lnRR_table <- data.frame(rho  = rho_range,
  "Overall effect" = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) coef(x)[1]),
  "Standard error" = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) x$se[1]),
  "p-value"        = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) x$pval[1]),
  "Lower CI"       = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) x$ci.lb[1]),
  "Upper CI"       = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) x$ci.ub[1]),
  "Log-likelihood" = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[1,1]),
  "AIC"            = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[3,1]),
  "BIC"            = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[4,1]),
  "AICc"           = sapply(SA_lnRR_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[5,1]),
  "Effect size"    = "lnRR")

# Table for SMDH values

SMDH_table <- data.frame(
  rho  = rho_range,
  "Overall effect" = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) coef(x)[1]),
  "Standard error" = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) x$se[1]),
  "p-value"        = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) x$pval[1]),
  "Lower CI"       = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) x$ci.lb[1]),
  "Upper CI"       = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) x$ci.ub[1]),
  "Log-likelihood" = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[1,1]),
  "AIC"            = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[3,1]),
  "BIC"            = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[4,1]),
  "AICc"           = sapply(SA_SMDH_VCV_range, function(x) fitstats(x)[5,1]),
  "Effect size"    = "SMD(H)"
)

# Combine and rename columns
table_combined <- bind_rows(lnRR_table, SMDH_table) %>%
  rename(`Sampling correlation` = rho)

# Create a gt table
table_combined <- table_combined %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Effect size") %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Sensitivity to sampling correlation (ρ)**"),
    subtitle = md("Results for lnRR and SMD(H) Meta-analytic models")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    `Sampling correlation` = html("&rho;"),
    `Overall.effect` = "Overall effect",
    `Standard.error` = "SE",
    `p.value` = "p",
    `Lower.CI` = "CI low",
    `Upper.CI` = "CI high",
    `Log.likelihood` = "LogLik"
  ) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "95% CI", columns = c("Lower.CI", "Upper.CI")) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c("Overall.effect", "Standard.error", "Lower.CI", "Upper.CI",
                "Log.likelihood", "AIC", "BIC", "AICc"),
    decimals = 4
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = "p.value", decimals = 3) %>%
  opt_table_outline() %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(13),
    data_row.padding = px(4)
  )

# Save table
gtsave(table_combined, here::here("tables/SA_sampling-correlation_table.png"))

# Combine CI and PI into a single column each for compactness
SA_intercept_only <- SA_intercept_only %>%
  mutate(
    CI = paste0("[", sprintf("%.3f", CI_Lower), ", ", sprintf("%.3f", CI_Upper), "]"),
    PI = paste0("[", sprintf("%.3f", PI_Lower), ", ", sprintf("%.3f", PI_Upper), "]"),
    P_value = scales::pvalue(P_value),
    Q_value = sprintf("%.2f", Q_value)
  ) %>%
  select(
    effect_size,
    data_used,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    PI,
    P_value,
    k_effect_sizes,
    n_studies)

# Let's make this table pretty

  gt() %>%
  tab_options(

Table: RoB Meta-regressions

# Loading models for blinding performed or not
lnRR_blinding <- readRDS(here::here("model/lnRR_blinding.rds"))
SMDH_blinding <- readRDS(here::here("model/SMDH_blinding.rds"))

# Loading models for random sampling assignment performed or not
lnRR_random_assignment <- readRDS(here::here("model/lnRR_random_assignment.rds"))
SMDH_random_assignment <- readRDS(here::here("model/SMDH_random_assignment.rds"))

# Loading models for missing data present or not
lnRR_missing_data <- readRDS(here::here("model/lnRR_missing_data.rds"))
SMDH_missing_data <- readRDS(here::here("model/SMDH_missing_data.rds"))
# Let's source our custom function to extract values from the meta-regressions
source(here::here("functions/extractor_metareg.R"))

## For lnRR Values
lnRR_results_RoB <- extractor_metareg(lnRR_blinding,"blinding") %>%
  bind_rows(extractor_metareg(lnRR_random_assignment,"random_assignment")) %>%
  bind_rows(extractor_metareg(lnRR_missing_data,"missing_data")) %>%
  mutate(effect_size = "lnRR")

## For SMDH Values
SMDH_results_RoB <- extractor_metareg(SMDH_blinding,"blinding") %>%
  bind_rows(extractor_metareg(SMDH_random_assignment,"random_assignment")) %>%
  bind_rows(extractor_metareg(SMDH_missing_data,"missing_data")) %>%
  mutate(effect_size = "SMDH")

## Now let's write the table for publication:
# Combine both results
combined_results_RoB <- bind_rows(lnRR_results_RoB, SMDH_results_RoB) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(moderator, level),
    names_from = effect_size,
    values_from = c(estimate, p_value, CI, PI, k, n),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{effect_size}"
  ) %>% # Prepare row labels to mimic grouping
  arrange(moderator, level) %>%
  mutate(row_type = "level")

# Final combined table with headers and levels
combined_results_RoB <- combined_results_RoB %>%
  # bind_rows(moderator_header ,combined_results) %>%
  arrange(moderator, row_type) %>% select(-row_type) %>%
  relocate(level, .after = moderator) %>%
  mutate(moderator = case_when(
    moderator == "blinding" ~ "1. Blinding",
    moderator == "random_assignment" ~ "2. Random assignment to treatment",
    moderator == "missing_data" ~ "3. Partial Reporting"
  )) %>%
  mutate(moderator = factor(
    moderator,
    levels = c(
      "1. Blinding",
      "2. Random assignment to treatment",
      "3. Partial Reporting"
    ))) %>%
  arrange(moderator) %>%
  mutate(level = case_when(
    level == "y" ~ "Yes",
    level == "n" ~ "No",
    .default = level))

# Clean up or reorder columns for display
# Select and order columns for clarity
RoB_table <- combined_results_RoB %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "moderator") %>%
  tab_header(title = md("**Multilevel Meta Regressions for Risk of Bias**")) %>%
  cols_label(
    # R2_marginal_lnRR = "R²_mar",
    # R2_marginal_SMDH = "R²_mar",
    level = "Level",
    estimate_lnRR = "Estimate",
    CI_lnRR = "95% CI",
    PI_lnRR = "95% PI",
    p_value_lnRR = "P-val",
    k_lnRR = "k",
    n_lnRR = "n",
    estimate_SMDH = "Estimate",
    CI_SMDH = "95% CI",
    PI_SMDH = "95% PI",
    p_value_SMDH = "P-val",
    k_SMDH = "k",
    n_SMDH = "n") %>%
  sub_missing(
    columns = everything(),
    missing_text = "") %>%
  opt_table_outline() %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = "small",
    heading.title.font.size = 12,
    table.border.top.width = px(2),
    column_labels.font.weight = "medium",
    row_group.font.weight = "bold") %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(
      sides = "bottom",
      color = "black",
      weight = px(1)),
    locations = cells_body()) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = c(p_value_lnRR),
      rows = p_value_lnRR < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = c(p_value_SMDH),
      rows = p_value_SMDH < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "lnRR", columns = contains("_lnRR")) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "SMDH", columns = contains("_SMDH"))  %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(whitespace = "nowrap"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = c(CI_lnRR, PI_lnRR, CI_SMDH, PI_SMDH)))
# saving the image
gtsave(RoB_table,here::here("tables/SA_RoB_table.png"))

# saving as a docx file or html
gtsave(RoB_table,here::here("tables/SA_RoB_table.docx"))
gtsave(RoB_table,here::here("tables/SA_RoB_table.html"))
